chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Mutayyil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Nahdi. He said: Thabit ibn Dinar al-Thumali narrated to us from the Master of Worshipers, Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said:

One day, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) looked toward Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who had come forward while a group of his companions were around him. So he said: Whoever wants to see Yusuf in his beauty, Ibrahim in his generosity, Sulayman in his splendor, and Dawud in his strength, then let him look at this one.

key_terms.بهجة: Splendor/delight — Sulayman (Solomon) is associated with regal majesty and divine blessing
key_terms.جمال: Beauty — Yusuf (Joseph) is Quranic tradition's archetype of beauty
key_terms.سخاء: Generosity — Ibrahim (Abraham) is renowned in tradition as the father of generous hospitality
key_terms.سيد العابدين: Master of Worshipers — the honorific title of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (the fourth Imam)
key_terms.قوة: Strength — Dawud (David) is renowned for martial and spiritual power

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Ali ibn Abi Talib comparing him to the prophets Yusuf, Ibrahim, Sulayman, and Dawud?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) pointed to Imam Ali (AS) and declared that whoever wishes to see the beauty of Yusuf, the generosity of Ibrahim, the splendor of Sulayman, and the strength of Dawud combined in one person should look at Ali ibn Abi Talib. This prophetic statement, transmitted through Imam Zayn al-Abidin from his father Imam Husayn, encapsulates the exceptional qualities of Imam Ali by comparing him to four prophets famed for those virtues. The original audience of early Muslims would have understood this as the highest possible praise, as each prophet named was renowned for a defining characteristic that set him apart.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Matil al-Daqqaq narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Sinan narrated to us from Ja`far b. Sulayman al-Nahdi. He said: Thabit b. Dinar al-Thumali narrated to us from the Master of Worshipers `Ali b. al-Husayn from his father (as). He said:

One day, the Messenger of Allah (s) looked to `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) and came forward while a group of his companions were around him. So, he said: He who wants to see Yusuf in his beauty, Ibrahim in his generosity, Sulayman in his delight, and Dawud in his strength should look to this one.
